what: Per-host access policy for scholarly retrieval by an agent. RULE-TIER asset (hooks/, requester-confirmation, git-tracked). Read by skills/literature-search-extract/connectors/access_policy.py (the skill's P2 routing + P4.5 access_route check), by skills/literature-search-extract/verify/fetchsrc.py (refuses before it fetches) and by hooks/literature_host_guard.py (machine-wide PreToolUse deny). Governing rule: rules/literature-access.md — this file is that rule's routing table made machine-readable; it never grants anything the rule forbids.
institution: National Taiwan University (the only entitlement this machine has been observed to carry — ops/environment.md §Institutional literature access). If the VPN resolves to another org, every institutional row here is void.
hard_rules: A challenge (202, 401, 403, 418, 429 on first request, a JS interstitial, a CAPTCHA, a proof-of-work page) is a ROUTING SIGNAL: stop, record the host as hand-to-user for this run, move on. Never retried with another User-Agent, cookie jar, headless browser or logged-in profile.
A row grants a SURFACE for a NAMED single document. No row grants crawling, searching a publisher's own index, or bulk retrieval.
The agent never enters credentials and never asks for the VPN to be switched on (connectors/README.md C7).
A measured challenge is a row, not a retry: a host that answered with bot management on 2026-09-10 is agent_banned until re-measured by the user.

surfaces.script: this skill's own scripts (fetchsrc.py, citecheck.py, connectors/*.py) — plain HTTP, identified User-Agent where consent exists
surfaces.webfetch: the harness WebFetch tool — plain HTTP, anonymous
surfaces.browser_headless: playwright-headless MCP or the in-app Browser pane — a browser without the user's login
surfaces.browser_user: claude-in-chrome — the user's real Chrome WITH their sessions; spends their authenticated identity

classes.open: open access or public data; any surface for a named document; full text may be retained
classes.metadata_api: an official programmatic interface (Crossref, Semantic Scholar, E-utilities, arXiv export…) — the licensed automation route; script/webfetch only
classes.landing_page: a publisher host whose terms permit viewing single pages; what is legally visible on the landing page (abstract, captions, references) at human pace; retention excerpt unless the item is OA
classes.agent_banned: the host's terms forbid robots/intelligent agents (IEEE Xplore ToU: 'access, search and/or systematically download') OR bot management answered with a challenge — hand the named article to the user; no surface
classes.institutional_only: reachable only as a Licensed User of the institution's subscription (WoS, Scopus, airiti, the library discovery layer) — the agent hands the user a query pack; no surface

unlisted_default.basis: rules/literature-access.md step 3 — ordinary HTTP retrieval of a NAMED target at human pace is ordinary web reading; a browser surface is NOT granted until a row lists it (user ruling R2, 2026-09-11)
unlisted_default.run_cap_note: more than 3 distinct unlisted hosts in one run is a sweep wearing a different name — stop and add rows first (design review 2026-09-11 finding 7/E3)

unmeasured_note: Subscription publishers this machine has not probed. They fall under unlisted_default (one script/webfetch of a named URL, no browser) and count toward the run cap; a measured challenge promotes one to agent_banned, a read ToU decides between landing_page and agent_banned.
review_when: the VPN resolves to a different institution · a listed host changes side (a new challenge, or a challenge that stops) · a publisher exposes an official TDM API (row gains tdm_api and the host may move to metadata_api for that route) · IEEE changes its Terms of Use · a host is added to browser-pane-allowlist.json (that list is about GPU blast radius, not licence — it settles nothing here)
